=============== I-1275 ===============
U2'S "WHAT A PROVER LANE CAN DO THIS ROUND" IS ALREADY DONE -- BOTH STEPS. The row still presents them as the bounded win available now, so a lane that takes the row at its word spends a round re-landing landed work.

MEASURED work-reviewer, fresh context, at HEAD on disk. Row: AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.divrep.u2, the run-0082 s0004 box.

THE PRESCRIPTION: "(i) root the file [Picard/DivisorFamilyAffThetaTyping.lean] (one import line) so the a = 0 separation is kernel-checked in-graph; (ii) re-state whichever DivisorFamilyAffTheta.lean declarations U2 needs over ThetaTrivData instead of ChartTyping, using ChartTyping.thetaTrivData so nothing breaks." The same box calls the file UNROOTED ("grep at HEAD: zero importers").

(i) STALE. AlgebraicJacobian.lean:346 imports AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyAffThetaTyping, and .lake/build/lib/lean/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivisorFamilyAffThetaTyping.olean exists (dated 2026-07-29 14:07). Rooted and kernel-checked in-graph.

(ii) STALE, and further than the row imagines. The file's own section "The Theta-layer, re-indexed on the chart-free datum" (from ~:352) already carries the WHOLE chain over ThetaTrivData, not a few declarations: trivDeltaRight, trivGluedSubmodule, mem_trivGluedSubmodule_iff, TrivGlued, trivPieceEval, trivEval, trivEval_apply, trivEval_mem, trivGluedEval, ker_trivGluedEval_eq_ker, germ_read_mem_stalkIdeal_of_trivEval_eq_zero, ker_trivGluedEval, trivWindowCarve, ker_trivWindowCarve, trivWindowCarve_surjective, and trivWindowQuotEquiv.

So the widened window quotient equivalence EXISTS over the chart-free index, conditional on nothing but Function.Surjective (trivGluedEval A T). All axiom-clean [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]: trivWindowQuotEquiv, ker_trivGluedEval, AffCoverData.thetaTrivDataZero, nonempty_thetaTrivData_and_isEmpty_chartTyping, ChartTyping.thetaTrivData.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN, unchanged: surjectivity of the widened evaluation (the (c2) transport), and the a > 0 producer of ThetaTrivData -- thetaTrivDataZero gives a = 0 only. Neither step closes U2, exactly as the row says; but neither is the step the row tells a lane to take.

ACTION: replace that box's two-step recommendation with the real residue (widened-evaluation surjectivity), and delete the "THE FILE IS UNROOTED" / "zero importers" sentences. Cross-check against I-1248, which independently reports the larger structural point that the Theta layer supplies only ONE input of IsDivRepClassify.
=============== I-1276 ===============
THE univSeed STRADDLING PROBE U2 SAYS "NOBODY HAS RUN IN TWO ROUNDS" IS THE WRONG QUESTION -- the seed's cover is chart-subordinate BY CONSTRUCTION, as a structure FIELD, so measuring its support decides nothing.

MEASURED work-reviewer, fresh context, by statement at HEAD. Row u2: "does univSeed's supportLocus meet both V0 and V1? ... it DECIDES whether the chart-typed class half is dead or merely open. Do it first."

THREE LANDED FACTS:
1. ThetaGeneratorSeed (Picard/DivSchemeFamily.lean:74) has field `side : relCurve C R -> Bool` plus `piece_le (z) : D.piece z <= relPinnedChart C R pi (D.side z)` (:98). Every piece sits inside ONE pinned chart.
2. `localEquations` (:349) sets cover := { opens := D.piece, ... }; localEquations_cover_opens is rfl. The LocalEquations the certificate is about has exactly those chart-confined pieces.
3. univSeed (Picard/DivRepChartClassUniv.lean:131) = highWindowPointwiseGeneratorSeed, side = `pointwiseSide z := (exists_mem_relPinnedChart z).choose` (Picard/DivSchemeSeedUnivPointwise.lean:89) -- confirming I-1248's trace.

So this seed family never yields a cover with a piece meeting both charts. The confinement is a field, not an accident, which is why no file compares its support to V0/V1: the no-go's hypothesis is about the COVER, and the cover is chart-typed a priori.

STRONGER OBSTRUCTION THE ROW DOES NOT CITE: isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart_of_isCertified (Picard/DivSchemeCertZarConfine.lean, DivisorAdaptation namespace, axiom-clean) forces BOTH chart traces of the support to be CLOSED with NO connectivity hypothesis. The row cites only the preconnected form (forall_not_isCertified_of_straddling).

BOUND ON SCOPE: the fibre-Weil part of univSeed's window divisors cannot straddle. fiberWeilDivisor_coeffAt_of_mem_chart-1 (RiemannRoch/FLVFiberToolkit.lean, AlgebraicGeometry ns) gives coefficient 0 at every non-generic point of fiberChart-1; the def's docstring says "Supported on V0 \ V1". Axiom-clean, re-applied in a scratch probe, lake env lean EXIT=0. Caveat I did NOT close: fiberTwoCover_V0/V1 = fiberChart0/1 by rfl (Cohomology/RigidEngine4Relative.lean:88), but relCover is a pullbackProd base change, so the bridge to the relative curve is one unclosed step.

ACTION: do not spend a round measuring univSeed's support. Restate the probe as: can any route to U2's class half present the divisor on a cover that is NOT chart-subordinate? ThetaGeneratorSeed.piece_le answers no for this family.
=============== I-1277 ===============
c9-chartlocus'S "Remaining: a PRODUCER of the per-affine-piece datum ... is not claimed" IS STALE, and so is Pic0ChartUnivReduce's in-file "no theorem in the tree produces haff for a general test. It is a genuine open obligation."

MEASURED work-reviewer, fresh context. Row AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-c.c9-chartlocus, updated_at 2026-07-29T11:20:26Z.

THE PRODUCER EXISTS AND POSTDATES THE ROW. exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range (Picard/Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:178) produces the per-affine-piece datum outright from range membership, via BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq (Cohomology/GluedSheafExtraction.lean:301). It is consumed by isOpen_chartLocus_of_isPlusHonest (:316) and packaged as DATA by chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest (:334). Ledger dates: Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean at ed39d62996 / 0743cf6e7b (2026-07-29 14:04 / 15:30 +0800), Pic0ChartHonestAff.lean at 03df3b87ba (2026-07-30) -- all AFTER the row's updated_at. Axiom-clean [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] vs a control (AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian) firing sorryAx.

WHICH CLASSES. Honesty producers exist for exactly the classes the chart layer reads: thetaFamily_isPlusHonest (:245), sigmaFamily_isPlusHonest (:256), abelDiv_isPlusHonest (:275), chartTwist_isPlusHonest (:294), and at the R2 carrier abelDivAff'_isPlusHonest / chartValueAff_isPlusHonest (Picard/Pic0ChartHonestAff.lean). So the CHART-side obligation is discharged; only honesty at an ARBITRARY picEt class remains, which is a different statement and is genuinely open.

THE haff SENTENCE. Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean's chartLocusOpens docstring still says haff is "a genuine open obligation" that "no theorem in the tree produces ... for a general test". False for any honest class: chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest is chartLocusOpens with haff discharged rather than passed through. I separately verified honesty RESTRICTS along a test morphism from Over.fromSpecAffine_naturality alone (see my I-1273), which is the general form of that bridge. I-1238 reports the same defect at the widened chart value; this is the general-honest-class version, and three sites still price it as owed.

ACTION: strike "Remaining: a PRODUCER of the per-affine-piece datum ... is not claimed" from the row's chart-u paragraph and replace with the arbitrary-class residue. Fix the chartLocusOpens docstring's "genuine open obligation" claim. NOT affected: c9b clause (ii) via IsChartLocusFibre's exists_factor, which is untouched by any of this.
=============== I-1278 ===============
DAT-B'S COVERAGE RESIDUE IS OVER-PRICED TWICE: the "0 <= Sigma legality" the files call "the open question" is not a hypothesis of the legality theorem at all, and the "reconciliation of the chart parameter with the threshold" is a PER-CHART calibration a landed theorem already absorbs.

MEASURED work-reviewer, fresh context, two scratch probes, lake env lean EXIT=0, axiom-clean [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] vs a control firing sorryAx.

(1) LEGALITY NEEDS NO EFFECTIVITY. Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean item 3 says the move is to let the index at parameter g carry the slack in Z, "whose own legality (0 <= Sigma) is the open question". But chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup (Picard/DivSchemeAbel.lean:382) takes ONLY deg_k Z = m*d1 - n -- no effectivity, no 0 <= Z. I closed the slack instantiation directly:
  chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup C pi (g+e) m Z ?_ T s   -- side goal by `rw [hZ]; push_cast; ring`
from hZ : deg_k Z = m*d1 - g - e. The "0 <= Sigma" question is about the DROP's output, and coverage has no drop (Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean's own point).

(2) THE CALIBRATION IS ALREADY PER-CHART. mixedParamRepresentableBy (Picard/Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:125) takes a per-index parameter nn : iota -> N with per-index (m i, Z i, hdeg i); its docstring states the engine never sees a chart parameter, so b = n is per-chart with no uniformity obligation. ledger_forces_b_eq_n then binds at each chart separately, and index_of_threshold satisfies it by construction. Axiom-clean.

REAL RESIDUE THAT SURVIVES: per test point, a divisor of the twisted fibre class over the splitting field with vanishing H1 -- DAT-0a at the fibre field. Not a reconciliation, not a legality question.

ALSO STALE ON THIS ROW: (a) the "separably closed level" coverage staging is off the live route -- IsSepClosed occurs in exactly 3 files tree-wide (Curve/SepPointsDense, SeparablyClosedPoints, SeparablyClosedFibre) and NO Picard coverage/chart-locus file imports that layer, since the drop-free route deleted the point oracle; (b) chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal (Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageAffineTest.lean, landed 2026-07-29 21:59 +0800, AFTER the row's updated_at 15:33Z) reduces the obligation to AFFINE tests, which the summary never mentions.

CAVEAT, measured not assumed: [Module.Finite] and [Algebra.IsSeparable] on mem_chartLocus_of_witness_h1 ARE load-bearing (both fail to synthesise when deleted); they come from exists_splitting_of_picEt's output, so structural, not chosen.
=============== I-1273 ===============
DAT-B'S ONE NAMED BRICK IS NOT NEEDED: "a spreading-out lemma for the RANGE of relPicToPicEt along a localisation A -> A_f" is FREE by naturality. The row prices it "genuinely absent ... not cheap, but bounded" and tells a lane to build it. A lane sent to build it would build nothing.

MEASURED work-reviewer, fresh context, scratch probes, lake env lean EXIT=0, axiom-clean [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] vs a control (AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian) firing sorryAx. Oleans verified newer than sources first, so no stale-import false success.

THE ROW'S CLAIM (dat-b summary, run-0082 s0006 box): the free passage is COVARIANT, the obligation CONTRAVARIANT, so you "would need the image to descend along relPic(A) -> relPic(kappa(t)), which is a spreading-out".

WHY NOT NEEDED. IsPlusHonest (Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:200) quantifies over affine opens U of T.left. The per-piece witnesses are RESTRICTIONS of one top witness, because picEtMap_relPicToPicEt (Picard/PicEtUnit.lean:194) IS naturality of the unit. Both close in three lines:
  probe_isPlusHonest_of_global (mu : picEt C T) (h : exists z, relPicToPicEt C T z = mu) : IsPlusHonest C T mu
    := by obtain <z, rfl> := h; intro U; exact <relPicMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) z, (picEtMap_relPicToPicEt C _ z).symm>
and hence, at an affine test, full openness with NO localisation step, via isOpen_chartLocus_of_isPlusHonest (:316).

I also closed the RESTRICTION form -- the shape c9's chartLocusOpens `haff` wants -- from Over.fromSpecAffine_naturality (PicEtUnit.lean:79) alone:
  honest_restrict_at (f : T' -> T) (h : IsPlusHonest C T mu) (U : T'.left.affineOpens) (V : T.left.affineOpens) (e : U.1 <= f.left ^-1 V.1) : exists z, relPicToPicEt ... z = picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T' U) (picEtMap C f mu)
    := by obtain <w,hw> := h V; exact <relPicMap C (Over.overSpecMap (Over.appLEAlgHom f V.1 U.1 e)) w, by rw [<- picEtMap_relPicToPicEt, hw, <- picEtMap_comp, <- picEtMap_comp, Over.fromSpecAffine_naturality f V U e]>
Needs attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra, else Algebra k Gamma(...) fails in the STATEMENT.

WHAT SURVIVES: honesty at an ARBITRARY picEt class is genuinely open and untouched. Only the ROUTE pricing is refuted -- the per-affine-piece quantifier costs zero given range membership at the top.

ACTION: strike the row's "CONSEQUENCE FOR A LANE ON THIS ROW" brick recommendation. The contravariance observation is right about the arbitrary-class gap, wrong about where the cost sits.

/-- **The Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor, bundled as a sheaf on the
big Zariski site** — the object mathlib's 01JJ local-representability engine
consumes. -/
noncomputable def pic0SigmaSheaf : Sheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u} (Type u) :=
  ⟨pic0SigmaFunctor C,
    (isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type _ _).mpr (pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf C)⟩

/-! ## The DAT-glue seam -/

/-- **The DAT-glue statement (worksheet §4, DAT-glue row)**: a chart family of
relatively representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf (DAT-C's
certificates) that is jointly Zariski-locally surjective (DAT-B's coverage) induces —
through mathlib's 01JJ engine and the stage-2 Σ-descent — a representation of the
type-valued degree-zero Picard functor by the glued scheme placed over the
Σ-component of the universal element.  The represented object's `.left` is
`(Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued` and its `.hom` is the universal
element's Σ-component, both definitionally. -/
noncomputable def pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
    {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)] :
    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
  (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).overSlice

end AlgebraicGeometry

/-- **A chart family whose chart parameter varies with the index.**

Each index `i` carries its own degree parameter `nn i`, its own representing object `D i` of
`divFunctor C π (nn i)`, its own twist exponent `m i` and chart index `Z i` — the latter legal
*at `nn i`*, i.e. `deg_k (Z i) = (m i)·d₁ − nn i`, which is what `chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup`

that it *typechecks*, i.e. that the target `pic0SigmaSheaf C` is parameter-free. -/
def mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens) (i : ι) :
    yoneda.obj ((V i : Scheme.{u})) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
  restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i)

variable (C π) in
/-- **Heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate**: the `hf` clause of a mixed-parameter
family is exactly a per-index `IsChartUniv`, by definition of both.

So a lane that can discharge CHART-U(c) *at one parameter* can discharge it index-by-index at
different parameters, with no additional compatibility between them — there is no coherence
condition across indices, because `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` imposes none. -/
theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
    (huniv : ∀ i, IsChartUniv C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) (V i)) (i : ι) :

/-- **A mixed-parameter chart family is admissible input to the DAT-glue seam.**

question `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack` and I-0660 both left implicit: the representability engine

    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))

`(C ⊗ overSpec k R).left`; see `AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.RelativeSectionsLinear`. -/

depth must be set in-file for the faithful per-file check. -/

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory TopologicalSpace
open Opposite

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

/-! ## The locally certified pin -/

variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
variable (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsAffineHom π]

/-- **The Addendum-2 frozen pin** (`informal/spec-dd-2.md`, Addendum 2): a
local-equation system on the relative curve is *locally certified* in degree `n` if
some span-⊤ family `g : Fin m → R` carries certified divisor families over the
localizations `Localization.Away (g i)` that are divisor-equal to the pulled system.
The pullback's regularity hypothesis is discharged once and for all by the Kit's
open-immersion lemma — the comparison of an away localization is an open immersion
(the S4 instance, provided by `haveI`). -/
def IsLocallyCertified (n : ℕ) (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) : Prop :=
  ∃ (m : ℕ) (g : Fin m → R), Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ i : Fin m,
      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) :=
        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i)) (g i)
      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C (Localization.Away (g i)) π n,
        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
          (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i)))
            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) d))

variable {C R π}

/-- **The locally certified pin respects divisor equality**: the local `DivEq`s
transport through `divEq_pullback` (regularity along the chart immersions is free). -/
theorem IsLocallyCertified.of_divEq {n : ℕ} {d d' : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
    (hd : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d) (h : Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d d') :
    IsLocallyCertified C R π n d' := by
  obtain ⟨m, g, hg, hG⟩ := hd
  refine ⟨m, g, hg, fun i => ?_⟩
  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) :=
    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i)) (g i)
  obtain ⟨G, hGdiv⟩ := hG i
  exact ⟨G, hGdiv.trans
    (Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i)))
      h _ _)⟩

/-- **A global certificate is a local one** (the trivial cover `g = ![1]`): the
certified part over `Localization.Away (1 : R)` is `mapAlg` of the family, whose
equations are the pulled system on the nose (`pulledEquations` IS the pullback along
the comparison; the regularity proofs are proof-irrelevant). -/
theorem CertifiedDivisorFamily.isLocallyCertified {n : ℕ}
    (F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) : IsLocallyCertified C R π n F.eqns := by
  refine ⟨1, fun _ => (1 : R), ?_, fun i => ?_⟩
  · have hrange : Set.range (fun _ : Fin 1 => (1 : R)) = {1} := Set.range_const
    rw [hrange, Ideal.span_singleton_one]
  · haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (1 : R))) :=
      isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (1 : R)) 1
    exact ⟨F.mapAlg (Localization.Away (1 : R)) n,
      Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl _⟩

12	# The fibre criterion at the RESTRICTED chart, and the `V`-coupling to coverage
13	
14	`Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean` reduces `IsChartUniv` — antecedent 1 of
15	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` — to `IsChartLocusFibre`.  **That reduction passes through the
16	unrestricted certificate, which the project's headers assert to be false**, and this file is
17	the repair.
18	
19	## The defect, measured
20	
21	`IsChartLocusFibre` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:166`) asks for a
22	`ChartFibrePresented C (abelSigmaChart …) g` at every test — the datum for the *unrestricted*
23	chart, with `W` a free structure field.  Nothing pins `W := chartLocus`, although the docstring
24	there says the `W` field "is already discharged — it is `chartLocus`".  So the open `V` never
25	enters the hypothesis, and one term gives back the unrestricted certificate:
26	
27	```
28	isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented _ fun T g => (h T g).some
29	  : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart …)
30	```
31	
32	That measurement is **not** repeated here: it is landed as
33	`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_abelSigmaChart_of_isChartLocusFibre` and
34	`mono_abelSigmaChart_of_isChartLocusFibre` in `Picard/Pic0ChartLocusFibreGuard.lean`, together
35	with `not_isChartLocusFibre_of_not_injective` — the criterion's own emptiness guard, finally
36	instantiated at the Abel chart.  In `isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` the restriction to `V` is
37	applied *after* the unrestricted certificate is in hand, so restricting buys nothing on the way
38	in.
39	
40	**The precise status of "false".**  `Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`, `Pic0ChartPair.lean:14` and
41	`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:214` all assert that the Abel chart is not injective (the
42	linear system `|D|`), and by the guard above that assertion makes `IsChartLocusFibre`
43	unsatisfiable.  But **no declaration proves the non-injectivity**: the guard takes
44	`¬ Function.Injective` as a hypothesis.  So `IsChartLocusFibre` is *conditionally* unsatisfiable
45	— dead if the headers are right, and nobody has shown they are.  This file therefore does not
46	claim the old route is dead; it claims the old route is gated on a proposition the project
47	believes false and has never checked, which is reason enough not to build on it.
48	
49	The criterion itself is **not** at fault: it is stated for an arbitrary morphism of presheaves
50	and is correct.  What was wrong is the *instantiation* — at `abelSigmaChart` rather than at
51	`restrictChart (abelSigmaChart …) V`.
52	
53	## What this file provides
54	
55	* `RestrictedChartFibre` — the same datum demanded at the **restricted** chart, so
56	  `exists_factor` only has to factor test points *of `V`*.
57	* `isChartUniv_of_restrictedChartFibre` — it gives `IsChartUniv` at that same `V`, one
58	  application of the existing criterion, with no unrestricted certificate in between.
59	* `necessity_of_restrictedChartFibre` — the weakening did not delete the content: the restricted
60	  datum still forces injectivity of the restricted chart on every test.
61	* `pic0RepresentableBy_of_restrictedChartFibre` — **the `V`-coupled assembly** (inbox `I-0861`):
62	  per-index restricted fibre data on the `hf` side, and on the coverage side the containment
63	  hypothesis `hV` of `Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.liftPointwiseToOpens`, together give the
64	  representation.  The two sides are made to share the same `V` by typing.
65	
66	## Division of labour with the two sibling files landed the same round
67	
68	`Pic0ChartLocusFibreGuard.lean` records why the *old* route must not be used, and
69	`Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.lean` supplies the **coverage** half of the `V`-coupling
70	(`liftPointwiseToOpens`, and the converse `pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart` showing `hV` is
71	exactly the gap).  This file supplies the **`hf`** half — the fibre datum at the restricted
72	chart — and the assembly that consumes both.  Nothing here re-proves either sibling.
73	
74	## The honest limits, stated rather than left for a reviewer
75	
76	* **Nothing here produces any input.**  This file replaces a badly-gated route by a
77	  well-gated one; it discharges no antecedent.  `rep` (divisor representability) is a hypothesis
78	  throughout, and `IsChartUniv` is not even statable without it.
79	* **`RestrictedChartFibre` at `V = ⊥` IS inhabited — settled in
80	  `Picard/Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean`, and an earlier draft of this section priced it
81	  wrongly.**  That draft said the `sq` field needs
82	  `Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (Over.mk a₁))` over an empty base, "the triviality of `picEt`
83	  over the empty scheme: true, a genuinely separate lemma, and absent from the tree", and
84	  concluded that *no satisfiability witness exists at any `V`*.  **Both the pricing and the
85	  conclusion were false.**  The error was in the reduction, not the census: the `congr 1` that
86	  peeled the Σ-component and named `pic0Subgroup` threw away the fact that `pic0SigmaSheaf` is a
87	  **sheaf**, and a sheaf's value at a scheme covered by the empty sieve is terminal.  So the goal
88	  is closed by `Sheaf.isTerminalOfBotCover` applied to `Scheme.bot_mem_grothendieckTopology`
89	  (both mathlib) with no fact about `picEt` at all — `restrictedChartFibre_bot`.  The
90	  `exists_factor` half is free as `I-0861` measured; `sq` is free for a different and cheaper
91	  reason than that draft supposed.
92	* **Consequence, and it is the sharp form:** the class is non-empty, so the repaired route is not
93	  a route to an uninhabitable hypothesis, and the unmeasured-inhabitation risk that `ChartTyping`
94	  (`I-0779`) and `IsChartLocusFibre` carried does **not** apply here.  What that inhabitant also
95	  shows is that `IsChartUniv` at `V = ⊥` is free (`isChartUniv_bot`) — antecedent 1 carries no
96	  content in isolation — while the coverage clause is *refuted* at that same value
97	  (`not_coverageContainment_bot`), and at the other end `V = ⊤` the prices are swapped: coverage's
98	  containment becomes free and this datum returns the unrestricted certificate.  So the obligation
99	  is the *coupling*, and any `V` that works must be a proper intermediate open.
100	* **What that does NOT establish, since a draft of this file claimed it did** (`I-1012`): the two
101	  endpoints are **not** a non-vacuity check for the assembly below.  Two *bad* values of `V` are
102	  two refutations; non-vacuity of the pair needs a `V` where both clauses hold.  Inhabitation of
103	  the **pair** is still unmeasured at every `V`, and `necessity_of_restrictedChartFibre` is not
104	  that check either.  Only `RestrictedChartFibre` *alone* is now known inhabited.
105	* **The relation to the old form IS measured, and an earlier draft mispriced it.**  That draft
106	  said the transport `IsChartLocusFibre → RestrictedChartFibre` "needs the preimage `r ⁻¹ V`
107	  pushed forward along `W.ι`, which is real work and buys nothing".  Both halves were wrong
108	  (`I-0936`): it is `restrictedChartFibre_of_isChartLocusFibre` below, twelve lines, needing only
109	  `IsOpenImmersion.lift` — and it buys the sharp statement, because its hypothesis is exactly the
110	  coverage half's `hV`.  The "buys nothing" clause was the worse error: a lane holding the old
111	  form gets `IsChartUniv` *through the certificate three headers call false*, which is this
112	  file's whole premise.
113	-/

178	side is free and the coverage side is impossible, so the two hypotheses cannot both be met at a
179	convenient `V`.
180	
181	Kept because it is the right thing to cite when asking what a producer of the datum must
182	establish — the relative form of DAT-C GAP-2, over `V` rather than over `D.left`. -/
183	theorem necessity_of_restrictedChartFibre {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
184	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
185	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
186	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
187	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
188	    (V : D.left.Opens) (h : RestrictedChartFibre C π n rep m Z hdeg V)
189	    (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
190	    Function.Injective
191	      ((restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) V).app T) :=
192	  injective_of_chartFibrePresented _ (fun T' g => (h T' g).some) T

194	/-! ## The transport, and what it says about the two halves of the coupling
195	
196	An earlier draft of this file priced this transport as "real work needing a pushforward" and
197	declined to prove it.  **That was wrong** (inbox `I-0936`): no preimage and no pushforward are
198	involved — keep the old datum's `W` and lift its `r` along `V.ι`. -/
199	
200	/-- **`IsChartLocusFibre` plus a range containment gives `RestrictedChartFibre`.**
201	
202	And the containment is the *same* one the coverage half owes: `hr` here is character-for-character
203	the `hV` of `Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.liftPointwiseToOpens`, asked on the fibre side instead of the
204	coverage side.  So the two halves of the `V`-coupling are **not two obligations** — they are one
205	range containment asked twice, from opposite directions.
206	
207	This is the sharp form of "the restricted datum is weaker", and it is what makes the repair
208	precise rather than merely differently-shaped. -/
209	theorem restrictedChartFibre_of_isChartLocusFibre {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
210	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
211	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
212	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
213	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
214	    (V : D.left.Opens) (h : IsChartLocusFibre C π n rep m Z hdeg)
215	    (hr : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
216	      Set.range (((h T g).some.r).base) ⊆ Set.range ((V.ι).base)) :
217	    RestrictedChartFibre C π n rep m Z hdeg V := by
218	  intro T g
219	  refine ⟨⟨(h T g).some.W, IsOpenImmersion.lift V.ι ((h T g).some.r) (hr T g), ?_, ?_⟩⟩
220	  · rw [restrictChart, ← Category.assoc, ← yoneda.map_comp, IsOpenImmersion.lift_fac]
221	    exact (h T g).some.sq
222	  · intro S v w hvw
223	    obtain ⟨u, hu1, hu2⟩ := (h T g).some.exists_factor S (v ≫ V.ι) w (by
224	      rw [← hvw, restrictChart]
225	      rfl)
226	    exact ⟨u, (cancel_mono V.ι).mp (by rw [Category.assoc, IsOpenImmersion.lift_fac]; exact hu1),
227	      hu2⟩

230	
231	variable (C π) in
232	/-- The `hf` clause of a mixed-parameter atlas, from per-index restricted fibre data.
233	
234	Named because the representing object of the assembly below mentions it. -/
235	theorem mixedParamHf {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
236	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
237	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
238	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
239	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
240	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
241	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
242	    (huniv : ∀ i, RestrictedChartFibre C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) (V i))
243	    (i : ι) :
244	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i) :=
245	  isChartUniv_of_restrictedChartFibre (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) (V i) (huniv i)
246	
247	variable (C π) in
248	/-- **THE `V`-COUPLED ASSEMBLY** — the composition inbox `I-0861` names as missing.
249	
250	Antecedents 1 and 2 of `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` are *not* independent.  Coverage produces a
251	point `x : (W : Scheme) ⟶ X i` of the chart **source**, which for the real atlas is
252	`(V i : Scheme)` — so coverage has to reach the very `V i` at which `hf` was certified, and no
253	statement in the tree said so.  Here they are forced to share `V` by typing: `huniv` certifies
254	the charts at `V`, and `hcov`'s witness lands in the same `V i`.
255	
256	**This closes no gate.**  `rep`, `huniv` and `hcov` are all hypotheses and none has a producer.
257	What the statement buys is that a lane discharging `hf` and a lane discharging coverage can no
258	longer each succeed at a *different* `V` and report the pair as composed. -/
259	def pic0RepresentableBy_of_restrictedChartFibre {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
260	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
261	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
262	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
263	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
264	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
265	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
266	    (huniv : ∀ i, RestrictedChartFibre C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) (V i))
267	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
268	      (Sigma.desc (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V))] :
269	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
270	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy
271	        (mixedParamHf C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V huniv)).homEquiv
272	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData
273	          (mixedParamHf C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V huniv)).glued)).1) :=
274	  pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V)
275	    (mixedParamHf C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V huniv)
276	
277	variable (C π) in
278	/-- **The same assembly with the local-surjectivity instance produced from coverage data**, so
279	that the shared `V` is visible in the hypotheses rather than hidden in an instance binder.
280	
281	The instance version above states the seam at the named representing object (which is what the
282	`JacobianData` layer consumes); this version is the one a *coverage* lane reads, because both of
283	its geometric hypotheses mention the same `V i`: `huniv` certifies the charts there, and `hcov`'s
284	range containment — `Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling`'s `hV` — puts the coverage witness there.
285	
286	The conclusion is stated as a `Σ` only because the named object above mentions the instance this
287	definition constructs; the representing scheme is the same one. -/
288	def pic0RepresentableBy_of_restrictedChartFibre_of_coverage {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
289	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
290	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
291	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
292	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
293	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
294	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
295	    (huniv : ∀ i, RestrictedChartFibre C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) (V i))
296	    (hcov : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
297	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ (D i).left),
298	        (abelSigmaChart C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)).app
299	            (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x
300	          = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s ∧
301	        Set.range (x.base) ⊆ Set.range ((V i).ι.base)) :
302	    Σ J : Over (Spec (.of k)), (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J :=
303	  letI : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
304	      (Sigma.desc (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V)) :=
305	    isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_of_pointwise C
306	      (fun i => abelSigmaChart C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) V hcov
307	  ⟨_, pic0RepresentableBy_of_restrictedChartFibre C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V huniv⟩
308	
309	end

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocusIsoInvariance
8	
9	/-!
10	# C9b: `IsChartUniv` reduced to one clause about the chart locus
11	
12	`Picard/Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean` splits `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` into the two
13	clauses mathlib's `MorphismProperty.relative` actually conjoins, and gives a criterion whose
14	input is elementwise.  This file instantiates that criterion at the Abel chart and at
15	`V := chartLocus`, which is the pair `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.
16	
17	The point is to make the residue **one named clause about the chart locus** instead of the
18	whole certificate.  Concretely, the criterion's `ChartFibrePresented` datum has four fields,
19	and at the Abel chart three of them are supplied here:
20	
21	| field | at the Abel chart | status |
22	|---|---|---|
23	| `W` | `chartLocus` of the test point's class, as an open | **shape supplied here**, but at the
24	  cost of `haff` — see the retraction below |
25	| `r` | the divisor family over the locus | the classifier `divRepClassifyZar` |
26	| `sq` | its class is the test's class | the classifier's own characterisation |
27	| `exists_factor` | uniqueness of the normalized representative | **the relative form of GAP-2** |
28	
29	So `W` needs only B-4 (**not** "nothing" — retracted below), `sq` is a property of whatever
30	`r` is, and the genuine content is
31	concentrated in `r` (a construction, from the classifier) and `exists_factor` (relative
32	GAP-2).  This file makes that split machine-checkable: `IsChartLocusFibre` below names
33	exactly the `r`/`sq`/`exists_factor` triple **at the chart locus**, and
34	`isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` proves `IsChartUniv` from it.
35	
36	## Why this is not a restatement
37	
38	A reduction that merely renames its obligation is worthless, and this one is checked against
39	that failure mode in two directions:
40	
41	* `chartLocusOpens` is **constructed**, not hypothesised, so the `W` field is a *shape* a lane
42	  no longer has to invent.
43	
44	  **RETRACTED 2026-07-29, second clause only** (`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean`).  This
45	  read "the `W` field costs zero, which is a real reduction of the datum from four fields to
46	  three".  The cost is not zero: `chartLocusOpens` takes the argument `haff`, and **nothing in
47	  the tree discharges it**.  `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` removed the
48	  `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` hypothesis but passes `haff` straight through, as does
49	  `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal` before it; the affine case that would feed it
50	  (`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation`) is itself conditional on
51	  `IsChartDatumPresentation`, which is dat-b row B-4's named residue and is only half landed.
52	  So the datum went from four fields to three *shapes* but not to three *obligations*.  The
53	  residue is now named `ChartLocusAffineLocal` and reduced to B-4's own obligation by
54	  `chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation`;
55	* `isChartLocusFibre_of_isChartUniv` is the **converse**: `IsChartUniv` at the chart locus
56	  gives injectivity on every test, so a lane cannot obtain `IsChartUniv` while avoiding the
57	  content of `exists_factor`.  The reduction is therefore an equivalence in the direction
58	  that matters, not a weakening.
59	
60	## Main declarations
61	
62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocusOpens` — `chartLocus` as an honest `T.Opens`, using the
63	  unconditional general-test openness.  This is the `V` that `restrictChart` wants.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsChartLocusFibre` — the residue: the `r`/`sq`/`exists_factor` triple
65	  of the criterion, at the chart locus, for every test point.
66	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` — **the reduction**: that triple
67	  gives `IsChartUniv` (hence the `hf` of the `(f, hf)` pair) at any open.
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.injective_of_isChartUniv` — the converse-direction check.
69	-/
70	
71	set_option autoImplicit false
72	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
73	
74	universe u
75	
76	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
77	
78	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
79	
80	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
81	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] {n : ℕ}
82	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
83	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
84	
85	noncomputable section
86	
87	/-! ## The chart locus as an open of the test
88	
89	`chartLocus` is a `Set T.left` and `restrictChart` wants a `T.Opens`.  The bridge is the
90	openness theorem.  **"which is now unconditional — so this costs a hypothesis-free definition
91	rather than a gate" is RETRACTED** (2026-07-29): the general-test openness theorem is
92	unconditional in `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` but still takes the affine-local `haff`, which
93	nothing discharges.  See `chartLocusOpens`' docstring and
94	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean`. -/
95	
96	variable (C) in
97	/-- **`chartLocus` as an open subscheme of the test.**
98	
99	For a test `T` presented as `Over.mk a` and a class `lam` on it, the chart locus is open by
100	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` (CHART-U(b) at a general test, unconditional since
101	`IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` was discharged), so it is an honest element of `T.Opens`.
102	
103	**THE `haff` SENTENCE HERE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED** (2026-07-29,
104	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean`).  It read: "The `haff` hypothesis is the affine-local
105	input of that theorem and is *not* a residue of this file: it is what the landed affine
106	openness supplies."  The landed affine openness does **not** supply it.
107	`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation` (`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean:321`) is conditional
108	on `IsChartDatumPresentation` — dat-b row B-4's own named residue, whose *witness* half is now
109	discharged too (`hconv`, by plus-unit injectivity,
110	`Picard/Pic0ChartPresentationConverse.lean`), leaving a plus-class base-change
111	identity — and no theorem in the tree produces `haff` for a general test.  It is a genuine
112	open obligation, named `ChartLocusAffineLocal` and reduced to B-4 by
113	`chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation`.  It is
114	carried as an argument here so the definition does not silently depend on a chosen route. -/
115	def chartLocusOpens (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
116	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T)
117	    (haff : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
118	      IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam))) :
119	    T.left.Opens where
120	  carrier := chartLocus C m Z lam
121	  is_open' := isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal' C m Z T lam haff
122	
123	@[simp]
124	lemma mem_chartLocusOpens {m : ℕ} {Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor}
125	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T}
126	    {haff : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
127	      IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam))}
128	    {t : T.left} :
129	    t ∈ chartLocusOpens C m Z T lam haff ↔ t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam :=
130	  Iff.rfl
131	
132	/-! ## The residue, named -/
133	
134	variable (C π n) in
135	/-- **The residue of C9b, named**: for every test point of the Σ-sheaf, the chart point over
136	its chart locus together with the two properties the criterion needs.
137	
138	**THE NEXT SENTENCE WAS FALSE AND IS RETRACTED (2026-07-29,
139	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusFibreGuard.lean`).**  It read: "This is `ChartFibrePresented` with its
140	`W` field already discharged — it is `chartLocus`, open unconditionally".  The `W` field is
141	**free**: it is a field of the structure, quantified inside the `Nonempty` below, and
142	`chartLocus` occurs nowhere in this definition — nor does `chartLocus` or `V` enter the proof
143	of `isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre`.  The criterion consumes the datum for the
144	**unrestricted** chart, so this statement implies
145	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart …)` at `V = ⊤`, hence `Mono`, hence injectivity on
146	every test — which `Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`, `Pic0ChartPair.lean:14` and
147	`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:214` all cite as FALSE for the Abel chart (its fibres
148	are the linear systems `|D|`).  If those headers are right this definition is
149	**unsatisfiable** and `isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre`, though sorry-free, can never fire.
150	See `not_isChartLocusFibre_of_not_injective` for the guard instantiated here, and inbox
151	`I-0874`.  A lane must decide that fork before attacking `exists_factor`.
152	
153	Modulo that retraction, what a lane owes is:
154	
155	* `r`: the divisor family over the locus whose class is the given one.  This is the
156	  classifier `divRepClassifyZar` applied to the canonical-section family, i.e. CHART-U(c)'s
157	  construction;
158	* `sq`: that its chart value *is* the given class, which is the classifier's characterising
159	  property;
160	* `exists_factor`: that two points with the same class agree, i.e. the **relative form of
161	  DAT-C GAP-2** (`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one` in families).
162	
163	Stated as a `Prop` over an arbitrary presenting datum rather than as a structure carrying the
164	family, because the family is the classifier's output and this lane must not guess its shape:
165	the existential is over morphisms of schemes only. -/
166	def IsChartLocusFibre {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
167	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
168	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
169	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ)) : Prop :=
170	  ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
171	    Nonempty (ChartFibrePresented C (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) g)
172	
173	/-- **THE REDUCTION**: the residue above gives `IsChartUniv`, hence the `hf` of the `(f, hf)`
174	pair, at *any* open of the divisor scheme.
175	
176	Two things are worth reading off the proof.  First, it goes through the criterion of
177	`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean` and then through the *composition* half
178	`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart` already landed in `Pic0ChartPair.lean` — so the two
179	halves of C9b compose exactly as the file headers predicted, with no seam.  Second, the open
180	`V` is arbitrary: restriction never has to be to the chart locus for `hf` to hold, because
181	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is stable under precomposition with an open immersion.  The chart
182	locus is where the *unrestricted* statement becomes true, which is a statement about
183	`IsChartLocusFibre`, not about `V`. -/
184	theorem isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
185	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
186	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
187	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
188	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
189	    (h : IsChartLocusFibre C π n rep m Z hdeg) (V : D.left.Opens) :
190	    IsChartUniv C π n rep m Z hdeg V :=
191	  isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart V
192	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented _ fun T g => (h T g).some)
193	
194	/-! ## The converse check: the reduction is not a weakening -/
195	
196	/-- **`IsChartUniv` forces elementwise injectivity of the restricted chart.**
197	
198	The converse direction of the reduction, and the reason it is a reduction rather than a
199	restatement: a lane that obtains `IsChartUniv` has, for free, the injectivity statement that
200	`ChartFibrePresented.exists_factor` is the hard half of.  So there is no route to `hf` that
201	avoids relative GAP-2 — the gate is real, and this file has moved it rather than removed it.
202	
203	Compare `isEmpty_forall_chartFibrePresented_of_not_injective`: that says the criterion cannot
204	be *satisfied* without injectivity; this says the goal cannot be *reached* without it. -/
205	theorem injective_of_isChartUniv {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
206	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
207	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
208	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
209	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
210	    (V : D.left.Opens) (h : IsChartUniv C π n rep m Z hdeg V) (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
211	    Function.Injective ((restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) V).app T) :=
212	  injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf h T
213	
214	end
215	
216	end AlgebraicGeometry

---
name: generic-degree-intuition-fails-at-the-pinned-degree
description: "Arguing \"h^0 >= 2 so the map is non-injective\" fails at the exact degree a construction pins, where the rank anchor forces h^0 = 1"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: a84c170a-6128-40b6-956b-1a69dba4e1d8
  modified: 2026-07-29T12:12:59.643Z
---

When judging whether a map out of a divisor scheme is injective, do NOT reason from the generic behaviour of linear systems. At the degree the construction actually pins, the numbers may be forced the other way.

Measured 2026-07-29 (run 0088, AJCR; refuted by ajcr-p3, I-0903): I argued the Abel chart is generically non-injective because the fibre is `|D| = P(H^0(O(D)))`, positive-dimensional when `h^0 > 1`. But the atlas reads at `deg D = g` (`chartTwist`'s target), and there with `Subsingleton H^1(O(D))` the rank anchor `h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one` (`AlgebraicJacobian/RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean:412`) forces `h^0 = deg + chi = g + (1 - g) = 1` **exactly**. The fibre is a single point precisely where it is used, so the `|D|` argument is unavailable at the only degree that matters.

**Why it matters beyond the slip:** three file headers in AJCR blame `|D|` for the unrestricted certificate's failure. They may be right that it fails and wrong about why — which relocates the whole question (to whether a divisor-scheme point can have non-vanishing `H^1`, i.e. to the carve). A wrong *reason* attached to a right *conclusion* survives every census and misdirects whoever prices the leaf next.

**How to apply:** before using a dimension/genericity argument, substitute the construction's pinned numerical values (degree, twist exponent, genus) and check whether an anchor identity collapses them. In this project the anchor is `h^0 = deg + chi` under fibrewise `H^1`-vanishing. Also: I asserted this to two lanes before checking, so the retraction cost three messages — verify the numerics before broadcasting a route judgement.

Related: [[converse-checked-reduction-can-still-be-false]] (same file, same session), [[goals-measure-difficulty-not-ingredients]], [[gap-count-vs-gap-cost]].
==========
---
name: subsingleton-not-finrank-for-vanishing
description: "State cohomology vanishing as Subsingleton (H¹ F), never as h¹ F = 0 — finrank reads 0 on infinite-dimensional spaces, so the finrank form is vacuously true and silently imports finiteness"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 17dacab2-7213-4998-90b2-32c4dd178a65
  modified: 2026-07-28T13:10:10.534Z
---

In these Lean algebraic-geometry projects, `Sheaf.h1 F` is `Module.finrank R (HModule F 1)`,
and `Module.finrank` returns `0` for an infinite-dimensional space. So `h1 F = 0` is
**vacuously true** exactly where vanishing is most in doubt, and any theorem concluding it
either needs a `Module.Finite` binder to mean anything or silently means nothing.

**Why:** stating vanishing as `Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule F 1)` is strictly stronger, and it
also turns out to need *less*: vanishing-propagation arguments go through surjectivity of a
cohomology map, which is not a dimension count. In AJC's
`RiemannRoch/Ledger/SectionDrop.lean` the entire H¹ peel chain (10 of 17 declarations) needed
neither `Module.Finite` binder — the unused-section-variable linter is what revealed it, not
foresight. The `finrank` spellings are the ones that require finiteness.

**How to apply:** conclude `Subsingleton (HModule F 1)` in the primary theorem and derive the
`h1 = 0` corollary separately, carrying the finiteness only there. When the linter reports an
unused instance binder on a vanishing lemma, treat it as a signal that the statement can be
strengthened, not as noise to silence with `set_option`. The same caution applies when reading
someone else's clean `#print axioms` line: a `finrank`-valued conclusion can be conditional in
a way axioms cannot see — see [[cross-project-lean-port-checks]].

## What this is NOT

This is the chart *map*, not a chart *atlas*.  Neither of the two properties
`JacobianData.ofCharts` needs is established here, and neither is available anywhere in the
tree today:

* `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart …)` is **false as stated for the whole divisor
  scheme** — the Abel map of a degree-`n` divisor scheme onto the Picard functor has projective
  spaces `|D|` as its fibres, so it is not a monomorphism, let alone an open immersion.  It

  point, i.e. where `h⁰ = 1`; that locus is the reserved `chartLocus` of `w4-datc` §3.3.

   `V`, and this is a *composition* of presheaf morphisms.  Landed here, sorry-free.

/-! ## The criterion is not vacuous

A structure whose hard field is an existential can be inhabited for trivial reasons, and a
criterion built on one is then worthless.  This section rules that out **by proof** rather
than by inspection: the datum is unconstructible exactly when it must be. -/

/-- **Non-vacuity of `ChartFibrePresented`, from the necessary direction.**

conclusion, and `exists_factor` is not a clause one can talk one's way past.

theorem isEmpty_forall_chartFibrePresented_of_not_injective {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ)
    (hT : ¬ Function.Injective (f.app T)) :
    IsEmpty (∀ (T' : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T' ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
        ChartFibrePresented C f g) :=
  ⟨fun D => hT (injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf
    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented f D) T)⟩

/-- The same statement in the form a lane will meet it: the criterion's input **implies**
elementwise injectivity on every test.  So a lane that cannot prove uniqueness of the
normalized effective representative cannot supply the datum either — the CERT-Σ gate is not
an artefact of how `IsChartUniv` was pinned. -/
theorem injective_of_chartFibrePresented {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (D : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
      ChartFibrePresented C f g) (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
    Function.Injective (f.app T) :=
  injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf
    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented f D) T

end

/-!
# DAT-J: the datum from a Pic⁰ representation and a surjective Abel map (DJ-1/DJ-2)

`informal/w4-datj-worksheet.md` §2.2 freezes the mechanism of `JacobianData.quasiCompact`:
*"a posteriori, `|J|` is the image of a quasi-compact divisor scheme under the Abel map."*
DJ-0 (`Picard/CompactImageQc.lean`) is the abstract engine and DD-Q's
`compactSpace_divScheme` is the compact source.  This file removes the remaining
bookkeeping between them, so the qc field costs exactly one surjectivity statement:

* `AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_of_surjective_from_divScheme` — **DJ-1's qc step**: a
  surjection from `DivScheme g` onto `J.left` gives `QuasiCompact J.hom`.  The compact
  source is the DD-Q instance, the base is affine, and DJ-0 does the rest; nothing about
  divisors or the Abel map enters, only that the source is *that* scheme.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofAbelImage` — **DJ-2**: the four-field packaging with the
  qc field replaced by the Abel-image hypothesis.  A producer owes a Pic⁰ representation, an
  lft certificate, and a point-surjective morphism out of `DivScheme g`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelImage` — the same against a chart atlas, so
  the infinite-atlas producer `ofChartsOfCompactSpace` (whose `CompactSpace` hypothesis is
  §2.1's genuinely a-posteriori one) becomes usable from a surjection.

**What this is and is not.**  It is the plumbing of §2.2 steps 1, 2 and 4, discharged once.
Step 3 — surjectivity of the Abel map on points — is DJ-1's honest brick and is *not* proved
here.  Per §0.5 that brick must stay Challenge-free: use `exists_effective_of_picClass` /
`riemann_inequality`, never `riemann_inequality_curve`, which imports `Challenge.lean`.

**AMENDMENT 2026-07-29, two corrections to the sentence this replaces.**  It used to say the
brick "needs the universal degree-`g` class, hence `divRep`, plus `exists_effective_of_picClass`
and the `fiberTwist` shift".  Both cost claims were wrong:

* **Not `divRep`-gated.**  The effectivity content is landed and divRep-free at every point of
  any `Pic⁰`-representing object (`exists_effective_deg_eq_of_pic0_at_point`,
  `Picard/JacobianDataAbelEffectivePoint.lean`).  Only the Abel *square* needs the
  representation.
* **No `fiberTwist` shift.**  At degree exactly `g` the entry condition `1 ≤ deg W + χ(𝒪)`
  reads `g ≤ deg W`, so the class sits on the boundary and `exists_effective_of_picClass` fires
  with no slack.  A shift is what one needs to lift a degree-*zero* class into the effective
  range, and that is one multiplication by a fixed degree-`g` class
  (`exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq_zero`), not a `fiberTwist` construction.

What genuinely remains on this side is **descent**: the divisor is produced over a finite
separable splitting field of `κ(y)`, and `hlift` wants `Spec κ(y)`.

Note that the statements below take the surjection as a *bare morphism* out of `DivScheme g`
rather than as an Abel map built from a representation.  That is deliberate: it keeps the
file independent of the divisor-representability chain, so the qc mechanism is available to
any producer of a surjection — including the chart-atlas route, which does not name an Abel
map at all.
-/

section Qc

variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsIntegral X]
variable (A B : X.CurveDivisor) (g r₁ r₂ : ℕ)
variable (b₁ : Module.Basis (Fin r₁) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k B ⊤))
variable (b₂ : Module.Basis (Fin r₂) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (A + B) ⊤))

/-- **DJ-1's quasi-compactness step** (w4-datj §2.2 steps 1, 2, 4): if the Jacobian-to-be
receives a point-surjective morphism from the divisor scheme `DivScheme g`, its structure
morphism is quasi-compact.

`DivScheme g` is a compact space (`compactSpace_divScheme`, DD-Q: it is a closed subscheme of
a Grassmannian pair with a finite affine atlas), the base `Spec k` is affine, and DJ-0's
`quasiCompact_of_surjective` converts a surjection out of a compact space into
quasi-compactness of the structure morphism.

brick and is not supplied here. -/
theorem quasiCompact_of_surjective_from_divScheme (J : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    (abel : DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ ⟶ J.left)
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective abel.base) :
    QuasiCompact J.hom :=
  quasiCompact_of_surjective abel J.hom hsurj

end Qc

/-! ## DJ-2: the packaging -/

section Package

variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsIntegral X]
variable {A B : X.CurveDivisor} {g r₁ r₂ : ℕ}
variable {b₁ : Module.Basis (Fin r₁) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k B ⊤)}
variable {b₂ : Module.Basis (Fin r₂) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (A + B) ⊤)}

/-- **DJ-2, the packaging** (w4-datj §1.1): the pinned Jacobian datum from a representation
of the degree-zero Picard functor, its locally-of-finite-type certificate, and a
point-surjective morphism from `DivScheme g`.

This is `JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy` with the fourth field replaced by the Abel-image
hypothesis, which is the form the classical construction produces: quasi-compactness of the
Jacobian is *not* structural (its atlas is infinite, §2.1) and has to come from the image
argument. -/
noncomputable def JacobianData.ofAbelImage (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom)
    (abel : DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ ⟶ J.left)
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective abel.base) :
    JacobianData C :=
  JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft
    (quasiCompact_of_surjective_from_divScheme A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ J abel hsurj)

@[simp]
lemma JacobianData.ofAbelImage_J (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom)
    (abel : DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ ⟶ J.left)
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective abel.base) :
    (JacobianData.ofAbelImage C J rep hlft abel hsurj).J = J :=
  rfl

end Package

The section above names the residue.  This one shows what it *is*, at a field, by exhibiting
the two hypotheses of DAT-C GAP-2's field keystone as consequences of class equality alone. -/

/-- **At a field, class equality delivers GAP-2's field keystone hypotheses on the nose.**

Two divisor families over a field `K` with equal Čech class have Weil divisors that are
**effective** (`zero_le_divFamDivisor`) with **equal Picard class** (`picClass_divFamDivisor`).
Those are exactly `hD`, `hD'` and `hcl` of `Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one`.

/-- **The split witness predicate** (CHART-U(a) in the `w4-datb` §1.6 (a-amendment)
spelling), at a plus class `μ` over a field `K`.

A plus class over a field need not be an honest Čech class — it is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for
an étale cover `E` of `K`.  The amendment's "for some finite separable `L/κ(t)` splitting
the collapsed plus class" is this: there is a finite separable extension `L/K` over which
`μ` becomes `relPicMk` of an honest Čech class `M` on `C_L`, and `M` admits an effective
witness divisor with vanishing `H¹`.

Stated with the witness clause on a *presenting Čech class* rather than on a datum,
because the datum layer is where the shifted-datum constructor (DAT-C GAP-1) is missing;
the two agree through `Pic0ChartLocusClass.mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_exists`.

## A convention this predicate INHERITS, and which a consumer must not misread

The worksheets say "effective degree-`g` witness with `h¹ = 0`".  The witness clause here —
and the tree's `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing`
(`Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:115`) that it mirrors, and the GAP-6 dictionary
`subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness` (`DivisorFamilyH1Locus.lean:182`) that both rest
on — asks for **neither `0 ≤ W` nor `deg W = g`**.  It asks only for a `CurveDivisor` in the
class with vanishing `H¹`.  That is deliberate on the tree's side: the dictionary is an *iff*
against the engine's complex-form condition `Subsingleton (H¹(pair D) ⊗ L)`, and that
condition cannot see effectivity or degree, so adding either clause would break the iff and
with it the openness route.

Two consequences, both load-bearing:

* the degree is supplied **externally**, by the chart-index constraint through
  `degAt_chartTwist` below: on a degree-zero `λ` the twisted class has fibre degree
  `m·d₁ − deg Z`, which the constraint `deg Z = m·d₁ − g` makes `+g`.  It is *not* a
  hypothesis of this predicate.  (Until 2026-07-28 this read `−g`, and that sign made the
  locus empty for every `g ≥ 1` — see `degAt_chartTwist` and issue I-0514;
  `chartTwist_chartValue` now pins the direction by the kernel);
* effectivity likewise is not asserted here.  Where the *worksheet's* stronger reading is
  actually needed — the canonical-section normalization `h⁰ = 1`, and GAP-2 uniqueness
  (`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one`, which does take `0 ≤ D`, `0 ≤ D'`) — the
  effectivity must be re-supplied at that point.  A lane that reads `IsSplitWitness` as
  already giving it will have a gap where it least expects one. -/
def IsSplitWitness {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L) (_ : Algebra K L)
      (_ : IsScalarTower k K L) (_ : Module.Finite K L) (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable K L)
      (M : (relCurve C L).CechPic),
    PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ)
        = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M)
      ∧ ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
          Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = M
            ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
                ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1)

/-!
# DJ-1, the topological half: point surjectivity from residue-field lifts

`Picard/JacobianDataAbelImage.lean` reduced DAT-J's quasi-compactness field to a single
statement, `Function.Surjective abel.base` — *step 3* of `informal/w4-datj-worksheet.md`
§2.2, the node's one honest brick.  §2.3 describes the argument for it in the language the
Picard theory supplies: *every field point of `J.left` is a degree-zero class over its
residue field, shift it by `fiberTwist`, take an effective representative, and that
representative is a `DivScheme`-point hitting the original point.*

That argument produces, for a point `y`, a **morphism** `Spec κ(y) ⟶ DivScheme g` — not an
element of the fibre of `abel.base` over `y`.  Nothing in the tree converted the first into
the second, and it is not bookkeeping that can be skipped: the target of DJ-1 is a statement
about the underlying *topological* map, while everything the Picard side produces is a
morphism of schemes.

This file supplies exactly that conversion, and nothing else:

> `surjective_of_forall_exists_residueField_lift` — if for every `y : Y` some
> `q : Spec (Y.residueField y) ⟶ X` satisfies `q ≫ f = Y.fromSpecResidueField y`, then
> `f.base` is surjective.

The proof is `Scheme.range_fromSpecResidueField` (mathlib): the range of
`Y.fromSpecResidueField y` is `{y}`, and `Spec κ(y)` is nonempty because `κ(y)` is a field,
so any point of `Spec κ(y)` maps into the fibre.  Composed with the DJ-0 lemmas this gives
the Jacobian datum producers in the shape the classical argument actually delivers: a
*per-point lift*, which is what `exists_effective_of_picClass` hands back.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_of_forall_exists_residueField_lift` — the conversion.
  Pure scheme topology; no curve, no Picard functor, no divisor scheme.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_of_forall_residueField_lift_from_divScheme` — DJ-1's qc
  step from per-point lifts.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofAbelLifts` and
  `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelLifts` — the two `JacobianData` producers
  with the surjectivity hypothesis replaced by per-point lifts.

## What this does NOT do

It produces no lift.  Producing one is the divRep-gated mathematics of §2.3 (the
`fiberTwist` shift plus `exists_effective_of_picClass`, which must stay Challenge-free per
§0.5 — `riemann_inequality`, never `riemann_inequality_curve`).  What changes is the shape
of that obligation: a lift *per point*, stated with no reference to `Function.Surjective`,
instead of a global surjectivity claim about a topological map.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

open CategoryTheory Limits

/-! ## The conversion: per-point lifts give surjectivity -/

section Topology

variable {X Y : Scheme.{u}}

/-- **Per-point residue-field lifts give point surjectivity.**  If every point `y` of `Y`
admits a morphism `q : Spec κ(y) ⟶ X` with `q ≫ f = Y.fromSpecResidueField y`, then the
underlying map of `f` is surjective.

`Spec κ(y)` is nonempty (a field is nontrivial), and the range of `Y.fromSpecResidueField y`
is `{y}` (mathlib `Scheme.range_fromSpecResidueField`), so the image under `q` of any point
of `Spec κ(y)` lies in the fibre of `f` over `y`.

This is the missing link between what the Picard side produces and what DAT-J's
quasi-compactness field consumes: `exists_effective_of_picClass` yields a *morphism* out of
a residue field, while `quasiCompact_of_surjective` wants a surjection of topological
spaces. -/
theorem surjective_of_forall_exists_residueField_lift (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (h : ∀ y : Y, ∃ q : Spec (Y.residueField y) ⟶ X,
      q ≫ f = Y.fromSpecResidueField y) :
    Function.Surjective f.base := by
  intro y
  obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ := h y
  -- a field is nontrivial, so `Spec κ(y)` has a point
  obtain ⟨s⟩ := (inferInstance : Nonempty (PrimeSpectrum (Y.residueField y)))
  refine ⟨q.base s, ?_⟩
  have hs : (q ≫ f).base s = (Y.fromSpecResidueField y).base s := by rw [hq]
  rw [Scheme.fromSpecResidueField_apply] at hs
  exact hs

end Topology

/-- **DJ-1's quasi-compactness step, from per-point lifts** (w4-datj §2.2 with step 3 in
the shape §2.3 delivers it): if every point of the Jacobian-to-be receives a
`DivScheme g`-valued lift of its residue-field point, the structure morphism is

`quasiCompact_of_surjective_from_divScheme`; the compact source is DD-Q's
`compactSpace_divScheme` instance, and the base is affine. -/

    (J : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    (abel : DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ ⟶ J.left)
    (hlift : ∀ y : J.left, ∃ q : Spec (J.left.residueField y) ⟶
      DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂,
      q ≫ abel = J.left.fromSpecResidueField y) :
    QuasiCompact J.hom :=

    (surjective_of_forall_exists_residueField_lift abel hlift)

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.JacobianDataAbelEffective
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartCoverageDegreeStep2
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartSplit

/-!
# DAT-J's effectivity input at a **point of the representing object**

`Picard/JacobianDataAbelEffective.lean` produced an effective divisor of degree `g` from a
class of degree `g`, and its satisfiability face
`exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq_zero` does it from a class of degree **zero** plus a
fixed degree-`g` reference divisor.  This file walks that back one further step, to the datum
DAT-J actually holds: a **point of `J`** together with the `Pic⁰` universal property.

## The chain, and where the divRep-gating actually starts

A point `y : J.left` of the representing object of `pic0TypeFunctor C` gives, with no choices:

1. the affine field test `Over.testPoint y : overSpec k κ(y) ⟶ J`
   (`Picard/Pic0ChartTestPoint.lean:176`) — mathlib's `fromSpecResidueField` read in the
   slice;
2. hence the restricted class `picEtMap C (testPoint y) λ` of any `λ : picEt C J`, and its
   fibre degree is `0` when `λ ∈ pic0Subgroup C J` (`mem_pic0Subgroup_iff`);
3. a finite separable `L/κ(y)` and a presenting Čech class `M` over `L`
   (`exists_splitting_of_picEt`, `Picard/Pic0ChartSplit.lean:143` — **unconditional** on the
   curve, which is what makes this file cheap);
4. `classDeg L M = 0` (`classDeg_presenting_eq_zero`,
   `Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageDegreeStep2.lean:98`);
5. and then this file's `exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq_zero`: an **effective divisor
   of degree `g`** over `L` presenting `M · 𝒪(Z)`.

**Nothing in 1–5 mentions the divisor-representability chain.**  So the "geometric half" of
DAT-J step 3 — the part `Picard/JacobianDataAbelSquare.lean` calls the honest Riemann–Roch
input `heff` — is *not* divRep-gated at all.  What *is* divRep-gated is the other half: that
the resulting `DivScheme`-point sits over `y`, i.e. the Abel-compatibility square, because
naming the Abel map at all requires the representation.

## The honest limit, stated because it is easy to overclaim here

The divisor produced below lives over the **splitting field `L`**, not over `κ(y)` itself, and
DAT-J's `hlift` wants a morphism out of `Spec κ(y)`.  Descending `L ↝ κ(y)` is a genuine
further step (finite separable descent — the `dat-g` lane's business), and this file does not
take it.  What it settles is that the effectivity content is available, unconditionally, at
every point of every `Pic⁰`-representing object.

## TWO FURTHER LIMITS, from a fresh-context audit of this file (`I-0802`, `I-0800`)

**(a) The reference divisor is quantified UNIFORMLY, which is strictly stronger than the
degree-`0` face asks.**  Because the splitting field `L` is produced *existentially inside the
proof*, the caller cannot name it in advance, so the hypothesis had to become
`Zof : ∀ L, (relCurve C L).CurveDivisor` together with `hZ : ∀ L, deg L (Zof L) = g` — a
degree-`g` divisor over **every** field extension at once, including `L = k`.  Compare the
single `Z` of `exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq_zero`.  This has **no producer anywhere
in the tree**, and it is unsatisfiable exactly when the index of the curve does not divide `g`
(`deg` is residue-degree weighted, `RiemannRoch/Divisor.lean:61`).  It is the *binding* limit of
this file — stronger than the descent limit named above, which is the one the first draft
disclosed.

**(b) A `PicRepDatum` face is NOT provided.**  The first draft of this docstring advertised
`PicRepDatum.exists_effective_deg_eq_at_point`, "the degree-zero class supplied by the universal
property rather than assumed".  **No such declaration exists** — it was never written, so the
one face that would consume the `Pic⁰` universal property is absent and `lam`/`hlam` remain
hypotheses the caller supplies.  Recorded rather than quietly deleted, because an advertised
declaration list is unchecked by any build.

**(c) The cone is NOT `Challenge`-free**, and `w4-datj-worksheet.md` §0.5/§3.4 make that

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyFieldSurj
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.JacobianDataFromPicRepDatum

/-!
# DAT-J step 3 is one compatibility square, not a construction

`Picard/JacobianDataFromPicRepDatum.lean` reduced DAT-J to two inputs: a
`PicRepDatum k k C` and, for every point `y` of the representing object, a lift

> `∃ q : Spec κ(y) ⟶ DivScheme g, q ≫ abel = fromSpecResidueField y`.

The lift has been read as "the Abel map is surjective on points", i.e. as geometry still
to be done. **The morphism half is already built**, in a rooted file, and what is missing
is only that it sits over the right point.

## What is landed, and had no consumer

`Picard/DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean` (rooted, sorry-free) carries the whole *fibrewise*
chain, and the reason it is short is that **over a field the certificate is free**:

* `DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_of_deg` (`:104`) — over a field `K`, an adaptation whose
  presentation divisor has degree `n` is `IsCertified n`.  All seven clauses: projectivity
  and both flat-cokernel clauses are `Module.Free.of_divisionRing` instances, `(c1)`
  finiteness is `moduleFinite_colength`, and the `(c2)` rank clause is the *unconditional*
  CRT identity `deg_presentationDivisor` read against the degree hypothesis.  No support
  separation is needed — which the file records as a deviation of record, since full
  support separation is unachievable when a support point lies in both charts' overlap.
* `exists_divFam_divFamDivisor_eq` (`:147`) — hence every effective degree-`g` divisor over
  `K` *is* the divisor of a `DivFam`.
* `effectiveDivisorClassifyZar` (`:217`) — and it classifies, giving
  `overSpec k K ⟶ divSchemeOver …`, characterized by `effectiveDivisorClassifyZar_spec`
  (`:231`).

This is the sharp form of critical-path §7.6's own observation that the `DivFamZar` no-go
is a purely *relative* phenomenon, **vacuous over a field**: the difficulty that makes U2
hard does not exist fibrewise.

## What is therefore actually missing

`effectiveDivisorClassifyZar_spec` says the morphism is `divRepClassifyZar` of a family
presenting `D`.  It says **nothing about `abel`**.  So joining it to `hlift` needs exactly
one statement — that classifying an effective divisor and then applying the Abel map
returns the class of that divisor's point:

> `AbelCompatible abel` : for every field point and every effective degree-`g` divisor `D`
> over it, `(effectiveDivisorClassifyZar … D …).left ≫ abel` is the morphism `Spec K ⟶ J`
> named by the class of `D`.

That is a *compatibility square*, not a surjectivity theorem, and it is the recorded
"groups agree ≠ maps agree" gap (inbox `I-0525`): a bijection between divisor classes and
`DivScheme`-points is unusable until the square relating the two named morphisms lands.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsAbelClassifyCompatible` — the square, as a named interface.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_residueField_lift_of_abelCompatible` — the square plus
  fibrewise effectivity gives the `hlift` obligation **verbatim** as
  `JacobianData.ofAbelLifts` / `PicRepDatum.toJacobianDataOfAbelLifts` consume it.

## What this does NOT do

It produces no `AbelClassifyCompatible` and no effectivity witness, so it builds no
`JacobianData`.  It removes the *construction* from DAT-J step 3 and leaves a square and
an effectivity input, both stated here rather than assumed anywhere.

## AMENDMENT 2026-07-29: `heff` is NOT the divRep-gated half

The text above calls `heff` "the honest geometric input", which is right, and the `dat-j`
roadmap row read that as work still gated behind divisor representability.  It is not:
`Picard/JacobianDataAbelEffective.lean` and `Picard/JacobianDataAbelEffectivePoint.lean`
discharge the effectivity content, at every point of *any* `Pic⁰`-representing object, with
no `divFunctor`, no `DivFamZar`, no certificate and no chart
(`exists_effective_deg_eq_of_pic0_at_point`).

So of the two halves this file separates, only the **square** is divRep-gated — naming
`abel` requires the representation.  They were never gated alike.  What the effectivity side
still owes is *descent*: its divisor lives over a finite separable splitting field of `κ(y)`,
and `hlift` wants `Spec κ(y)` itself.
-/

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivRepAffPullClause

/-!
# U2 as an equation between morphisms: the chart maps lie in the range of the classifier

`Picard/DivRepAffPullClause.lean` reduced the whole divisor-representability chain to a
single hypothesis, `DivRepChartFamily.IsChartClause U`, and `IsChartClause.of_id` showed
that its `ω`-quantifier collapses to the identity point, i.e. to the DDR9-U ε-identity as
`informal/w4-ddr9-worksheet.md` §3.1 states it.  That is still a *submodule* identity with
a `∀`-quantifier over tower tests and framings hidden inside `IsDivRepClassify`.

This file removes that quantifier.  The backward classifier `divRepClassifyZar`
(`Picard/DivRepClassifyZar.lean`) is defined for **every** locally certified class over
**every** affine test, unconditionally, and `isDivRepClassify_unique` says it is the
*only* morphism satisfying the clause.  So the clause is not an extra property at all:

> `IsDivRepClassify F₀ v` ↔ `(divRepClassifyZar … F₀).left = v`.

Both directions are one line — forward is uniqueness, backward is a rewrite — and the
consequence is that U2 becomes an **equation between two morphisms of schemes that both
already exist**:

> U2 ↔ for each pair chart `(i, j)`, `(divRepClassifyZar … (U i j)).left = ChartMap i j`.

Reading off the existential, the last obligation of divisor representability is that
each chart map lies in the **range** of the classifier at its own chart ring:

> `divFunctor_representableBy_of_chartRange` :
>   `(∀ i j, ∃ F, (divRepClassifyZar … F).left = ChartMap i j) →`
>   `(divFunctor C π g).RepresentableBy DivOver`

Since `divRepClassifyZar` is injective on classes (`eq_of_isDivRepClassify`,
`Picard/DivRepClassifyZarSep.lean`), representability of `divFunctor` is *equivalent* to
surjectivity of `divRepClassifyZar` at every affine test; what this file records is that
surjectivity at the **chart rings alone** suffices.  That is the honest content: the
classifier is already a bijection onto its range everywhere, and the whole remaining debt
is that the finitely many chart points are hit.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.isDivRepClassify_iff_divRepClassifyZar_left_eq` — the clause **is**
  the classifier equation, in both directions.  General: no chart family, no universal
  point.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivRepChartFamily.isChartClause_iff_forall_classify_eq` — U2 as a
  per-chart equation of morphisms, **as an iff**, so it is a reduction and not merely a
  restatement (the safeguard of inbox `I-0571`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFunctor_representableBy_of_chartRange` — divisor
  representability from range membership of the chart maps.

## What this does NOT do

It produces no class over a chart ring, so it clears no gate: U2 is unproved and, per
roadmap `…divrep.u2`, the production of a chart class with the tautological ε remains the
G-4 obligation.  What changes is what a producer has to exhibit — a class whose classifier
*is* the chart map, rather than a family satisfying a quantified submodule identity.  The
=== variables ===
*is* the chart map, rather than a family satisfying a quantified submodule identity.  The
endpoint also still carries `hO`, `hχ` and the ambient curve instances.
-/

-- `relCurve` `def` barrier, so they are installed locally exactly as in
-- `Picard/DivSchemeSeedUnivAssembleKappa.lean` and `Picard/JacobianDataAbelEffective.lean`.
